about: Known reasons a Zcash wallet shows zero or loses access after a restore or a network upgrade, with what to try; none of these steps ever needs your seed or keys on a website.

rows.symptom: I restored my Zodl (Zashi) seed in another wallet and my balance is zero or too small.
rows.when: restoring a Zodl or Zashi seed in another wallet
rows.advice: Wallets keep change at different addresses, so a restore can miss coins. In the Zkool app choose Restore account, open Advanced Options and make sure 'Use Internal Change' is on (it is by default). Set a birth height at or before your wallet's start: 2419000 covers any wallet created in Zashi, and a phrase that is older than that needs an earlier height. Let it sync fully. Zingo 3.0 or later also reads Zodl seeds. Type your seed only into the wallet app on your own device, never into a website or for someone who messages you.

rows.symptom: I opened my Zashi or Zodl seed in Cake Wallet and some of my ZEC is missing.
rows.when: restoring a Zashi or Zodl seed in Cake Wallet
rows.advice: Cake can't see the one-time addresses Zodl uses for sends to TEX addresses (such as Binance deposits) and for swap refunds, so ZEC sitting there doesn't show. Restore the seed in Zodl, Zingo or Zkool instead; Zodl itself finds those one-time addresses. If you want to use Cake, create a new Cake wallet and send your balance to it from the wallet that shows it.

rows.symptom: Zodl showed my balance, then after the Ironwood migration (or an app update) it shows zero and no history.
rows.when: after the in-app Orchard to Ironwood migration or an app update
rows.advice: First check your recovery phrase is written down and matches what Zodl shows. Then resync: on iOS delete and reinstall Zodl, on Android use Zodl's resync steps. If it is still zero, restore the same phrase in Zkool ('Use Internal Change' on, early birth height) or Zingo. If both still show zero, email support@zodl.com; forum cases like this were still open in October.

rows.symptom: YWallet no longer works or won't send my ZEC.
rows.when: after the Ironwood upgrade (NU6.3, July 2026)
rows.advice: YWallet dropped Zcash support at Ironwood and its developer points users to Zkool, which comes from the same developer. Install Zkool, choose Restore account, enter your YWallet seed in the app, set an early birth height and let it sync. You don't need to change 'Use Internal Change': with it on, Zkool still finds YWallet's change. Type your seed only into the wallet app on your own device.

rows.symptom: The Zcash MetaMask Snap won't open or shield, and I can't reach my ZEC.
rows.when: since the Ironwood upgrade; the Snap's NU7 update was still unreleased on 9 Nov 2026
rows.advice: Your coins stay on the chain. MetaMask approved the Snap's Ironwood release on 4 Nov 2026, and its NU7 update is being audited. The maintainers say that update will show recovery words that open the funds in Zodl or Zkool. Update the Snap (now called 'Zcash WebZjs Wallet') from MetaMask's Snaps directory when it arrives. Never type your MetaMask secret recovery phrase into a website or 'recovery tool', and ignore anyone who messages you offering help.

rows.symptom: I have an old transparent private key (often starting with K or L) and no wallet will import it or show the balance.
rows.when: importing a paper or exported transparent key from an old wallet
rows.advice: Zkool can import an old transparent private key (starting with 5, K or L). If the import says the account has no transparent key, turn 'Use Internal Change' off and import again (fixed in Zkool's code on 5 Nov, not yet in a release). If the key imports but syncing stops with 'too many transactions', the address has a very large number of small payments: set the birth height to around your first payment instead of 1, so the search is smaller. Zallet can't import a bare key yet; it only helps if you still have a zcashd wallet.dat file. Nobody needs your key to help you: never send it to anyone who offers help, and if a key is very old or was ever shared, treat it as public and move the coins to a new wallet.

rows.symptom: I restored my old Trust Wallet seed and my ZEC isn't there.
rows.when: restoring an old (for example 2020) Trust Wallet seed
rows.advice: Trust Wallet shows only some coins after a restore, so first add ZEC to the coin list in Trust Wallet and wait for it to load. If it still shows nothing, the forum's advice is to restore the seed in Zkool, which reads only the Zcash part. That seed also controls your other coins, so move those with Trust Wallet first if you can, and type it only into the app on your own device. Trust Wallet only shows coins you add with 'Manage crypto', so add Zcash there first. To send ZEC from Trust Wallet after NU7 (6 Nov 2026), update the app: older versions build a transaction format the network now rejects. If you restore the seed in Zkool instead, install it only from its GitHub releases or the official app stores, and remember the seed also controls your other coins.

rows.symptom: My old zc... (Sprout) ZEC can't be moved any more.
rows.when: since NU7 (block 3,543,405, 6 Nov 2026), which froze about 12,224 ZEC still in Sprout
rows.advice: Sprout coins are not destroyed, but no software can spend them now and no recovery plan has been approved. Keep your old wallet.dat or keys backed up offline and follow the Zcash forum for any future recovery proposal. Transparent t1 coins from the same era are not frozen and can still be moved. Anyone offering to 'unfreeze' Sprout for you is a scam.

rows.symptom: My Zodl send to Binance failed and the money isn't back in my balance.
rows.when: sending from Zodl to a tex1 (Binance) address
rows.advice: Zodl first moves the coins to a one-time transparent address it owns, then on to Binance; if the second step fails, the coins wait there. In Zodl's Activity, open the transaction just before your send (0.00015 ZEC) and copy its t1 address (not Binance's tex1). Turn on Tor protection, then in Settings long-press the ZODL logo to open Discover Funds, paste the t1 address and tap Scan address.

rows.symptom: A swap or CrossPay payment from Zodl failed and I never got my ZEC back.
rows.when: swapping or paying through NEAR Intents inside Zodl
rows.advice: Refunds are usually automatic to the refund address set when the swap was made. If 24 hours have passed with nothing back, look up your swap's deposit address or transaction ID on explorer.near-intents.org and file a request with NEAR support through the link in Zodl's help article; manual refunds can take a couple of days. You never need to give anyone your seed for a refund.

rows.symptom: My Keystone won't sign and I can't migrate or move my shielded ZEC.
rows.when: after the Ironwood upgrade (NU6.3) on Keystone firmware older than 3.0.2
rows.advice: Update the Keystone to the Cypherpunk firmware 3.0.2 or later (by microSD or USB, following Zodl's guide), then sign the migration or send again from Zodl. Your seed stays on the Keystone the whole time. On 9 Nov a later bug was still open: firmware 3.1.x and 3.2.0 reject Zodl's larger signing requests with "Invalid QR Code" (see the next cause), while 3.0.4 accepts them.

rows.symptom: My Keystone scans the whole animated QR from Zodl and then says ‘Invalid QR Code’.
rows.when: signing a large Zodl transaction (an Ironwood migration, or a send that spends many notes) on Keystone firmware 3.1.x or 3.2.0
rows.advice: Your coins haven't moved. Firmware 3.1.0 added a size check that rejects signing requests over about 14 KB, and Zodl's larger requests are bigger than that; the same request scans on 3.0.4. The bug was reported to Keystone and was still open with no fixed release on 9 Nov. Watch Keystone's release notes for the fix; a smaller send (fewer notes in one transaction) may fit under the limit, but a migration can't always be split. Your seed stays on the Keystone throughout.

rows.symptom: Shielded ZEC I sent to my Brave Wallet never showed up, though the explorer says it went through.
rows.when: receiving shielded ZEC after the Ironwood upgrade (NU6.3)
rows.advice: New shielded payments now land in the Ironwood pool, and Brave turned Ironwood support on by default in version 1.97.56 (7 Oct 2026). Update Brave on desktop and let the Zcash account sync fully. If the funds still don't show, use 'Reset ZCash sync state' at brave://settings/web3, then let it sync again. If that doesn't help, open a ticket with Brave support.

rows.symptom: My send fails with 'incorrect consensus branch id' and the coins never leave.
rows.when: after a network upgrade (NU6.3 in July, NU7 on 6 Nov 2026) in a wallet or signer that hasn't updated
rows.advice: Nothing is lost: the network refused a transaction built with old rules, so the coins never moved. Since NU7 the error usually says the transaction version is invalid, or names the consensus branch ID. Update the wallet app and any hardware firmware (Vultisig Android is fixed in 1.0.124; Trust Wallet needs its latest version). If your device gets no update (Ledger stopped updating apps for the original Nano S), restore its 24 words on a supported Ledger such as a Nano S Plus, Flex or Stax. Don't type a hardware wallet's words into a phone or desktop wallet unless you first move your other coins: those words protect everything on the device.

rows.symptom: Zkool's Ironwood migration is stuck at 'Waiting 0s' and makes no progress.
rows.when: running Zkool's Orchard to Ironwood migration
rows.advice: This was a known Zkool bug when a small leftover Orchard amount (about 0.005 to 0.0062 ZEC) fell in a 'dead zone'. It was fixed in Zkool 6.29.0; the current release is 6.36.0. Update Zkool and run the migration again. If it still stalls, lock that small leftover note in coin control and run it again.

rows.symptom: My shielded (Sapling) ZEC on my Ledger, from the old 'Zcash Shielded' app, can't be moved since NU7, and Ledger Wallet doesn't show it.
rows.when: since NU7 (6 Nov 2026), for Sapling funds held through the Zondax 'Zcash Shielded' Ledger app (used with YWallet or Zkool)
rows.advice: Your coins are still on the chain. The old Zondax app can't sign the transactions the network accepts since NU7, and Ledger's new Zcash app and Ledger Wallet don't show Sapling funds at all, so no Ledger device can move them now. The route left is your Ledger's 24 words: Zondax derived these Sapling keys its own way, so most wallets won't find them, but Zkool can. Those words also protect everything else on that Ledger, so first move your other coins to a wallet with a different recovery phrase. Then, in Zkool on your own computer, choose Restore account, turn on Advanced Options and the H/W Ledger switch, pick 'Zondax (Sapling)', enter the words, set a birth height from before your first Sapling payment, and let it sync. Install Zkool only from its GitHub releases or the official app stores. Nobody needs your words to help you.

rows.symptom: Ledger Wallet (Ledger Live) on my phone says 'Unsupported transaction version' when I try to send old transparent ZEC.
rows.when: sending transparent ZEC from Ledger's mobile app when the coins arrived in a very old transaction (from before October 2018) or in one that also carried Sapling shielded data
rows.advice: Nothing is lost: the send was refused before anything left. Ledger's mobile app still uses an older signing path that reads the transaction your coins came from, and very old formats fail there. Send from Ledger Wallet on a desktop computer instead, version 4.21 or later, with the Zcash (ZEC) app 3.9.4 or later installed from My Ledger: Ledger says the desktop path doesn't read that old transaction. This works on a Nano S Plus, Nano X, Flex, Stax or Nano Gen5; the original Nano S isn't supported. Your 24 words stay on the device the whole time.

rows.symptom: I restored my old seed (for example from a Ledger) but coins I received before late 2018 never show up.
rows.when: restoring a seed whose first ZEC arrived before Sapling activated (block 419,200, October 2018)
rows.advice: Zodl and Zingo won't scan from before block 419,200 and raise an earlier birth height to that block, so older payments are never found. If the coins are on a Ledger, first try sending them from Ledger Wallet on a desktop computer (4.21 or later, with the Zcash app 3.9.4 or later): Ledger says that path no longer reads the old transaction, and your 24 words stay on the device. Otherwise restore the seed in Zkool with birth height 1; since these are transparent coins you can turn off the shielded pools to make the sync quicker. If Zkool shows the balance but says 'No feasible note selection found', the note is probably locked in coin control: unlock it and send again. A Ledger's 24 words also protect your other coins, so before typing them into Zkool on your own device, move those coins to a wallet with a different recovery phrase.

rows.symptom: I sent ZEC from my shielded wallet to Binance and it was never credited.
rows.when: sending from a shielded balance straight to a Binance deposit address, which only takes coins sent from a transparent address
rows.advice: If the transaction confirmed on the chain, the coins reached Binance: it holds deposits that come from the shielded pool instead of crediting them. Open a ticket with Binance support, give them only the transaction ID and the amount, and ask for the deposit back to a transparent (t1) address you control. Binance has returned such deposits after an internal audit, but it gave no date in September 2026, and earlier cases on the forum took from one to several weeks. Next time, send to Binance's tex1 deposit address from a wallet that handles TEX, such as Zodl, which makes the transparent hop for you.

rows.symptom: My old ZecWallet Lite won't open or sync, and the command-line version crashes with 'Couldn't get network'.
rows.when: opening a ZecWallet Lite or zecwallet-cli wallet (unmaintained since about 2023)
rows.advice: Your coins are still on the chain. ZecWallet Lite hasn't been maintained since about 2023 and its default server no longer runs, so the app can't connect or sync. Argos, a desktop recovery app from Sovright, reads ZecWallet Lite seed phrases and ZecWallet Lite wallet files (including encrypted ones), checks the extra addresses ZecWallet made, and sweeps the funds to an address you choose. Download it only from Sovright's GitHub releases and run it on your own computer. Never send the wallet file or seed to anyone offering to help, even for a fee.

rows.symptom: Zallet won't import my old zcashd Sapling key: z_importkey drops the connection, or the key imports and shows nothing.
rows.when: moving a legacy zcashd Sapling spending key (secret-extended-key-main…) into Zallet beta
rows.advice: Zallet is still in beta, and on 4 Nov 2026 its developers confirmed that funds received to an imported Sapling key can't yet be spent, even in beta.4. Zkool imports a zcashd Sapling spending key directly: choose Restore account, paste the key into the app on your own computer, set a birth height from before your first payment and let it sync. Argos, a desktop recovery app, also scans and sweeps these keys and zcashd wallet.dat files. Keep the original wallet.dat backed up offline, and never send the key or the file to anyone who offers help.

rows.symptom: I paid someone in BTC (or another coin) from Zodl, they sent the payment back, and it never reached me.
rows.when: using Zodl's Pay (NEAR Intents) to pay an exchange or service that later returns the payment
rows.advice: The swap itself finished, so it isn't refunded automatically. The returned coins went back to the address that sent them, which belongs to the swap service, not to you. Contact NEAR's support through the form linked in Zodl's 'How do I obtain a refund for my swap?' article, and give them the swap's deposit address (t1…), the swap ID and the return transaction on the other chain. Zodl's team has offered to pass the deposit address on as well. Whether NEAR can send it back is up to them. To avoid this, pay exchanges from a wallet you control on that chain, not straight from a swap.

rows.symptom: Zodl has been stuck at the same sync percentage for days or weeks.
rows.when: syncing Zodl (reported on the latest version in September 2026)
rows.advice: First make sure your recovery phrase is written down and matches what Zodl shows. Then try another server: in '...' > More > Advanced Settings > Choose a Server, pick one of the fastest. If it still stops, resync: on iOS delete and reinstall Zodl; on Android use '...' > More > Advanced Settings > Reset Zodl and restore with your phrase. If it still won't finish, restore the same phrase in Zkool ('Use Internal Change' on, birth height 2419000 or earlier) or in Zingo, on your own device. Email support@zodl.com with your app version; never post your phrase anywhere.

rows.symptom: I restored my Cake Wallet seed in another wallet and ZEC I received at Cake's 'Transparent (Disposable)' addresses is missing.
rows.when: restoring a Cake Wallet ZEC seed in a different wallet
rows.advice: Cake makes its disposable transparent addresses from your seed plus a hidden extra passphrase that only Cake adds, so no other wallet finds coins sent there. Restore the seed in Cake Wallet itself, with a restore height from before those payments, and keep the app open until it has synced: Cake then shields what sits at those addresses into your wallet, unless the total is 0.0003 ZEC or less. Then send the balance to an address in your new wallet.
